entry.label: Systems laws
entry.description: Systems laws and principles are recurrent statements about patterns, constraints and dynamics in systems. They support disciplined inquiry but do not operate as context-free prescriptions or deterministic predictions.
entry.canonical_definition: A maintained domain of named systems patterns, laws and principles whose wording, scope and practical use must be inspected rather than invoked as slogans.
entry.public_stub_text: Research stub. Systems laws is included because it appears in one of the mapped source sets, but a reliable public explanation has not yet been written.

profile.title: Systems laws
profile.canonical_definition: Systems laws and principles are recurrent statements about patterns, constraints and dynamics in systems. They support disciplined inquiry but do not operate as context-free prescriptions or deterministic predictions.
profile.summary: Systems laws and principles name recurrent constraints and dynamics that can sharpen inquiry. Their practical value depends on wording, boundary, context and the question being asked.
profile.why_it_matters: The atlas already had 33 public law entries, but the containing domain was hidden as metadata. Making it public helps readers distinguish a law corpus from a book, a method and a practitioner.
key_distinctions: law or principle vs deterministic equation
named regularity vs evidence in a case
common_misreadings: a named law proves a conclusion
all systems laws have the same status
open_checks: record provenance and rival formulations for all 33 entries
distinguish scientific law, theorem, heuristic and practitioner principle
profile.editorial_note: Developed from cited public sources. The entry remains open to correction, rival accounts and stronger evidence.
